policies.name: Two gates
policies.desc: Gate 1 decides whether an artifact EXISTS for a viewer (component 13, audience). Gate 2 decides which ROWS a viewer sees inside it (component 12, data scope). They are independent: a viewer can be correctly entitled and correctly see zero rows.

policies.name: Counts are computed
policies.desc: Every count on this screen — "sees 8 of 60" — is derived from the roster at paint time. No count is stored. A stated count stops being true the moment the roster changes and nothing notices.

policies.name: Rule shape
policies.desc: A person is full-scope, or restricted by exactly one BASIS field plus the values of it they may see. A separate boolean mask hides row-level money while leaving totals visible.

policies.name: Legal basis
policies.desc: A field qualifies as a restriction basis only if every one of its values maps to a definite, non-empty set of the roster. Continuous measures — forecast, EAC variance, percent complete — are excluded: a rule on them re-resolves every week, which makes it a filter, not an access rule.

policies.name: No approval
policies.desc: There is no approval queue. Publishing, granting and revoking are immediate and logged. (Superseded the earlier CAPEX draft, which carried a six-item approval queue.)

policies.name: Admin holds none
policies.desc: The platform administrator administers entitlement and does not thereby acquire it. Their zero scope is by design, not omission.

policies.name: Publishing never widens
policies.desc: Adding a reader to an artifact grants existence, never rows. The reader opens it under their own rule.

plan.vw_project_plan_capex.label: Row
plan.vw_project_plan_capex.description: Row ordinal in the source extract. Positional only; it is not a business key and it does not survive a re-sort of the file.

plan.vw_project_plan_capex.label: Project Code
plan.vw_project_plan_capex.description: Project code, the primary business key for a capital project. Two shapes are in use: a discrete code (C24B535_651) and a blanket code (CZZF50310_658). The trailing segment after the underscore is the business-unit number.

plan.vw_project_plan_capex.label: Project Description
plan.vw_project_plan_capex.description: Free-text project description. Convention is project code, a site abbreviation and a short scope phrase. Human-authored, so the convention is followed but not enforced.

plan.vw_project_plan_capex.label: Region
plan.vw_project_plan_capex.description: Operating region. Four operating regions plus Shared Services Division, which is an organisational bucket rather than a geography and carries the sentinel state No State.

plan.vw_project_plan_capex.label: Business Unit
plan.vw_project_plan_capex.description: Business unit, formatted as BU number, a hyphen and the BU name. Each business unit belongs to exactly one region.

plan.vw_project_plan_capex.label: State
plan.vw_project_plan_capex.description: State. Each region maps to exactly one state. No State is a sentinel carried by Shared Services Division, not a missing value.

plan.vw_project_plan_capex.label: Budget Category
plan.vw_project_plan_capex.description: Budget category, the finance-side classification of the project. Six values in this extract, drawn from the attribute master's fifteen. Maps one-to-one to Program Affiliation, Budget Category 2 and High-Level Category.

plan.vw_project_plan_capex.label: Program Affiliation
plan.vw_project_plan_capex.description: Programme affiliation. Derived from Budget Category: PFAS maps to Federal PFAS Program, Lead maps to Lead Program, everything else to No program affiliation.

plan.vw_project_plan_capex.label: Asset Class
plan.vw_project_plan_capex.description: Asset class. Water Treatment, Water Network, Water Customer service lines, Overheads.

plan.vw_project_plan_capex.label: Project Manager
plan.vw_project_plan_capex.description: Project manager, as a person name. The source system carries two naming conventions in the same column - First Last and Last,First - and both appear here.

plan.vw_project_plan_capex.label: In_Phase
plan.vw_project_plan_capex.description: Delivery phase. In Planning, In Development, In Delivery. Agrees with Project Status at column 175.

plan.vw_project_plan_capex.label: WIN Approval Level
plan.vw_project_plan_capex.description: WIN approval level, Level 01 through Level 05. Populated only where the project has been through a WIN meeting.

plan.vw_project_plan_capex.label: WIN Approval Date
plan.vw_project_plan_capex.description: Date of the WIN approval meeting.

plan.vw_project_plan_capex.label: WIN Meeting Type
plan.vw_project_plan_capex.description: Meeting type for the WIN approval. Single-valued in this extract - every populated row reads Win Meeting - so the column carries no information beyond the fact of approval.

plan.vw_project_plan_capex.label: Start Date

plan.vw_project_plan_capex.label: Start Date (Adjusted)

plan.vw_project_plan_capex.label: End Date

plan.vw_project_plan_capex.label: End Date (Adjusted)

plan.vw_project_plan_capex.description: Active budget plan - the approved amount currently in force for the project. In the source this is the plan row whose status is Active, selected from a version chain by most recent approval date.

plan.vw_project_plan_capex.description: Most recent budget plan - the latest plan row in the chain, whether or not it is the one in force. Differs from Active Budget Plan wherever a newer plan has been submitted but not yet approved.

plan.vw_project_plan_capex.label: Optimized FY32
plan.vw_project_plan_capex.description: Optimized FY32 profile. Preserves the working total across FY26 to FY32 while re-phasing it across the years.

plan.vw_project_plan_capex.label: Large Project
plan.vw_project_plan_capex.description: Large-project flag. In the source this means the project carries a discrete project code rather than a blanket code - it is not a budget-size test.

plan.vw_project_plan_capex.label: Budget Category 2
plan.vw_project_plan_capex.description: Second budget-category rollup, one-to-one with Budget Category with PFAS relabelled to Federal PFAS Program.

plan.vw_project_plan_capex.label: High-Level Category
plan.vw_project_plan_capex.description: High-level category - the executive-facing rollup. Projects, PFAS, Blankets (minus Lead) and roll-ups, Lead, Overhead.

plan.vw_project_plan_capex.label: Project Status
plan.vw_project_plan_capex.description: Project status with an ordering prefix - 1-In Planning, 2-In Development, 3-In Delivery. Agrees with In_Phase at column 10.

plan.vw_project_plan_capex.label: Approved Indicator
plan.vw_project_plan_capex.description: Whether the project has an approved budget plan. YES, NO, or null where no plan row exists.

plan.vw_project_plan_capex.label: ITD vs. Active Budget Plan
plan.vw_project_plan_capex.description: Inception-to-date actuals as a share of the active budget plan. Null where no active plan exists.

plan.vw_project_plan_capex.column_id: FY26 Actual vs. FY26 Working Budget
plan.vw_project_plan_capex.label: FY26 Actual vs. FY26 Working Budget
plan.vw_project_plan_capex.description: FY26 actuals as a share of the FY26 working budget. Null where the working budget is zero.

plan.vw_project_plan_capex.label: Start Date (Effective)
plan.vw_project_plan_capex.description: Effective start date - the adjusted start where one exists, otherwise the original.

plan.vw_project_plan_capex.label: Start Year
plan.vw_project_plan_capex.description: Start year, taken from the effective start date.

plan.vw_project_plan_capex.label: End Date (Effective)
plan.vw_project_plan_capex.description: Effective end date - the adjusted end where one exists, otherwise the original.

plan.vw_project_plan_capex.label: End Year
plan.vw_project_plan_capex.description: End year, taken from the effective end date.

plan.vw_project_plan_capex.label: Unencumbered
plan.vw_project_plan_capex.description: Whether the project's budget is unencumbered - no approved plan row is in force against it.

plan.vw_project_plan_capex.label: Asset Risk Assessment
plan.vw_project_plan_capex.description: Asset risk assessment, sentinels removed. Tolerable Risk or Intolerable Risk, null where no assessment was made.

plan.vw_project_plan_capex.label: Asset R&P Assessment
plan.vw_project_plan_capex.description: Combined asset risk and performance assessment, formatted as risk, a slash, then performance.

plan.vw_project_plan_capex.label: Priority Level - Approved
plan.vw_project_plan_capex.description: Priority level where the budget plan is approved. Constant 1 wherever populated, so the column distinguishes nothing beyond approval status, which column 176 already carries.

plan.vw_project_plan_capex.label: Priority Level - Compliance
plan.vw_project_plan_capex.description: Priority level derived from the compliance driver.

plan.vw_project_plan_capex.label: Priority Level - Asset Risk
plan.vw_project_plan_capex.description: Priority level derived from the asset risk assessment. Null where no assessment was made.

plan.vw_project_plan_capex.label: Priority Level - Surcharge
plan.vw_project_plan_capex.description: Priority level derived from surcharge eligibility.

plan.vw_project_plan_capex.label: CAPEX Priority Level
plan.vw_project_plan_capex.description: Overall CAPEX priority level - the strongest of the component priority levels. Because its inputs are intent-derived, so is this.

plan.vw_project_plan_capex.label: x
plan.vw_project_plan_capex.description: Scratch column. The source's own working formula, reproduced literally: VECTOR plus Budget YTD plus the January budget. It has no business meaning and no unit that survives the addition.

plan.vw_project_plan_capex.label: y
plan.vw_project_plan_capex.description: Scratch column. The source's own working formula, reproduced literally: most recent budget plan less active budget plan. Negative wherever the newer plan is smaller.

plan.vw_project_plan_capex.label: Derived Row Flag
plan.vw_project_plan_capex.description: Row flag, constant True across the extract.

gl.vw_project_inservice.label: Logical Inservice Date
gl.vw_project_inservice.description: The logical in-service date the register carries for planning. Constant 2026-12-31 across every row in this extract, so it distinguishes nothing.

gl.vw_project_inservice.label: NEEDS TO BE UPDATED
gl.vw_project_inservice.description: Whether the in-service position is known to be out of date. True on every row whose estimated in-service date is null.

gl.vw_project_inservice.label: in_service_method
gl.vw_project_inservice.description: How the in-service position was set: Date, meaning a specific date was given, or Monthly, meaning it was set at month granularity.

gl.vw_project_inservice.label: Project Code
gl.vw_project_inservice.description: Project code. The join key back to vw_project_plan_capex. 260 of these codes have no matching project in the extract.

gl.vw_project_inservice.label: Budget Category
gl.vw_project_inservice.description: Budget category, duplicated from the project attribute master. Agrees with the project extract for every matched code.

gl.vw_project_inservice.label: Estimated In Service Date
gl.vw_project_inservice.description: Estimated in-service date — when the asset is expected to enter service and begin earning a return. Null wherever the update flag is set.

docs.document_corpus.label: document_id
docs.document_corpus.description: Document filename inside the project folder. Convention is contract number, document type and counterparty; scope documents break the convention.

docs.document_corpus.label: project_code
docs.document_corpus.description: Project code the document belongs to, taken from the folder name and confirmed against the document body. The join key from an unstructured document into the structured graph.

docs.document_corpus.label: document_title
docs.document_corpus.description: Document title as printed on the first page. Five distinct titles across the corpus.

docs.document_corpus.label: document_type
docs.document_corpus.description: Document class inferred from the title and form: owner-contractor agreement, owner-engineer agreement, project scope document.

docs.document_corpus.label: ejcdc_form
docs.document_corpus.description: EJCDC standard form number: C-520 and C-521 for construction agreements, E-500 for engineering agreements. Null on scope documents and on the non-standard agreements.

docs.document_corpus.label: contract_number
docs.document_corpus.description: Contract number. Prefix identifies the project, C or E identifies the discipline, and the sequence is per project.

docs.document_corpus.label: counterparty_contractor
docs.document_corpus.description: Contracting firm named as Contractor in the agreement. Twenty distinct firms across the corpus.

docs.document_corpus.label: counterparty_engineer
docs.document_corpus.description: Engineering firm named as Engineer in the agreement. Null where the document names no engineer.

docs.document_corpus.label: effective_date
docs.document_corpus.description: Effective date of the agreement, as printed. Stored in the source as a formatted string rather than a date.

docs.document_corpus.label: notice_to_proceed_date
docs.document_corpus.description: Notice-to-proceed date. Null on 61% of the corpus — the notice is a separate document that may not be filed with the agreement.

docs.document_corpus.label: contract_price_at_award
docs.document_corpus.description: Contract price as awarded — the committed amount at execution, before any change order.

docs.document_corpus.label: contract_price_as_adjusted
docs.document_corpus.description: Contract price as adjusted — the awarded price plus every executed change order. This is the figure that should be compared to a budget, and it is not the one printed on the first page.

docs.document_corpus.label: change_order_count
docs.document_corpus.description: Number of executed change orders found against the contract. Zero on scope documents and on contracts with no changes.

docs.document_corpus.label: project_manager_name
docs.document_corpus.description: Project manager named on the document, with title and organisation. A person name in a document body.

docs.document_corpus.label: business_unit_line
docs.document_corpus.description: Business unit line as printed — BU number, name, region and state. Two punctuation variants of the same line appear in the corpus.

docs.document_corpus.label: page_count
docs.document_corpus.description: Page count of the document as filed.

docs.document_corpus.label: is_scope_document
docs.document_corpus.description: Whether the document is a project scope document rather than an executed contract. Five of the thirty-six.

docs.document_corpus.label: active_budget_plan_stated
docs.document_corpus.description: Active budget plan as printed on the scope document. Present only on scope documents.

docs.document_corpus.label: most_recent_budget_plan_stated
docs.document_corpus.description: Most recent budget plan as printed on the scope document.

docs.document_corpus.label: value_under_contract_stated
docs.document_corpus.description: Total value under contract as printed on the scope document, across all contracts for the project.

docs.document_corpus.label: signature_block_names
docs.document_corpus.description: Names appearing in the execution and signature blocks — owner signatory, contractor signatory and witness.

docs.document_corpus.label: scope_text
docs.document_corpus.description: Full extracted body text of the scope document. Present on scope documents only.

docs.document_corpus.label: folder_name
docs.document_corpus.description: Drive folder name — project code, a space-hyphen-space and the project name. The folder convention is what carries the project association.

docs.document_corpus.label: extraction_confidence
docs.document_corpus.description: Confidence that the contract entity extracted from this document is correct. The lowest extraction confidence in the graph.

plan.plan_scenario_dim.label: SCENARIO
plan.plan_scenario_dim.description: The Scenario member key, as the cube stores it.

plan.plan_scenario_dim.label: SCENARIO NAME
plan.plan_scenario_dim.description: What the scenario is called on screen - Budget, Actual, Forecast.

plan.plan_scenario_dim.label: SCENARIO TYPE
plan.plan_scenario_dim.description: Whether the member holds a plan, a recorded actual, or a forecast vintage.

plan.plan_scenario_dim.label: DEFAULT VERSION
plan.plan_scenario_dim.description: The version this scenario resolves to when a form does not name one.

plan.plan_scenario_dim.label: IS ACTIVE
plan.plan_scenario_dim.description: Whether the scenario is open for input.

plan.plan_scenario_dim.label: EFFECTIVE FROM
plan.plan_scenario_dim.description: First period the scenario accepts data for.

plan.plan_capital_gate_log.label: PROJECT ID
plan.plan_capital_gate_log.description: The project the decision was made against. Declared as an identifier here, which is what lets the Data Modeling tab suggest the join.

plan.plan_capital_gate_log.label: GATE NUMBER
plan.plan_capital_gate_log.description: Which gate in the stage sequence. Derived class: measure.

plan.plan_capital_gate_log.label: DECIDED ON
plan.plan_capital_gate_log.description: When the gate was decided. Derived class: date.

plan.plan_capital_gate_log.label: APPROVED AMOUNT
plan.plan_capital_gate_log.description: What the gate released, in dollars.

plan.cw_project_master.label: PROJECT ID
plan.cw_project_master.description: The capital project key. Joins to cw_project_gate_log.project_id.

plan.cw_project_master.label: PROGRAM ID
plan.cw_project_master.description: The programme this project is funded under. Joins to cw_program_master.program_id.

plan.cw_project_master.label: VENDOR ID
plan.cw_project_master.description: The primary delivery contractor. Joins to cw_vendor_master.vendor_id.

plan.cw_project_master.label: PROJECT NAME
plan.cw_project_master.description: What the project is called on a filing and in the portfolio register.

plan.cw_project_master.label: LIFECYCLE PHASE
plan.cw_project_master.description: Where the project sits in the stage-gate sequence: Define, Execute, Commission, Closed.

plan.cw_project_master.label: AUTHORIZED AMOUNT
plan.cw_project_master.description: The approved capital envelope for this project, in dollars.

plan.cw_project_master.label: IN SERVICE DATE
plan.cw_project_master.description: When the asset is expected to go into service. No class stated here so it is read from the type.

plan.cw_project_master.label: IS ACTIVE
plan.cw_project_master.description: Whether the project is still open for spend. Derived class: flag.

plan.cw_program_master.label: PROGRAM ID
plan.cw_program_master.description: The programme key, as the budget cube stores it.

plan.cw_program_master.label: PROGRAM NAME
plan.cw_program_master.description: The programme's name - Water Treatment Renewal, Distribution Mains, and so on.

plan.cw_program_master.label: APPROVED ENVELOPE
plan.cw_program_master.description: The programme's total approved capital envelope across its projects.

plan.cw_program_master.label: PORTFOLIO OWNER EMAIL
plan.cw_program_master.description: Who owns the programme. Marked PII, so it answers the PII chip in the dictionary.

plan.cw_vendor_master.label: VENDOR ID
plan.cw_vendor_master.description: The vendor key as procurement issues it.

plan.cw_vendor_master.label: VENDOR REGION
plan.cw_vendor_master.description: The operating region the vendor is contracted to work in.

plan.cw_project_gate_log.label: PROJECT ID
plan.cw_project_gate_log.description: The project the decision was made against. Declared as an identifier here, which is what lets the tab suggest the join.

plan.cw_project_gate_log.label: GATE NUMBER
plan.cw_project_gate_log.description: Which gate in the stage sequence this decision closes. Derived class: measure.

plan.cw_project_gate_log.label: DECIDED ON
plan.cw_project_gate_log.description: When the gate was decided. Derived class: date.

plan.cw_project_gate_log.label: RELEASED AMOUNT
plan.cw_project_gate_log.description: What the gate released against the envelope, in dollars.

plan.plan_project_budget.label: PROJECT CODE
plan.plan_project_budget.description: The capital project key. The column the Data Modeling joins on this dataset are declared on.

plan.plan_project_budget.label: VERSION
plan.plan_project_budget.description: The budget version this row belongs to. Joins plan_version_master.Version.

plan.plan_project_budget.label: SCENARIO
plan.plan_project_budget.description: The cube Scenario member the amounts are held under - Budget for this table.

plan.plan_project_budget.label: FISCAL YEAR
plan.plan_project_budget.description: The fiscal year the amounts fall in, as the cube spells it (FY26).

plan.plan_project_budget.label: ENTITY
plan.plan_project_budget.description: The cube Entity member - the business unit that carries the budget.

plan.plan_project_budget.label: ACCOUNT
plan.plan_project_budget.description: The cube Account member. Joins plan_account_dim.Account.

plan.plan_project_budget.label: PHASE
plan.plan_project_budget.description: The project phase the amount is planned in. Joins plan_phase_dim.Phase.

plan.plan_project_budget.label: RESOURCE
plan.plan_project_budget.description: The resource member the amount is planned against. Joins plan_resource_dim.Resource.

plan.plan_project_budget.label: APPROVED BUDGET
plan.plan_project_budget.description: The approved capital envelope for this project and year, in dollars.

plan.plan_project_budget.label: WORKING BUDGET
plan.plan_project_budget.description: The envelope after in-year moves - what delivery is working to.

plan.plan_project_budget.label: BOARD APPROVED AMOUNT
plan.plan_project_budget.description: What the board paper released, where one exists for this year.

plan.plan_project_budget.label: CARRYOVER BUDGET
plan.plan_project_budget.description: Unspent authority carried in from the prior year.

plan.plan_project_budget.label: CONTINGENCY
plan.plan_project_budget.description: The contingency held inside the working budget.

plan.plan_project_budget.label: ESCALATION
plan.plan_project_budget.description: The escalation allowance inside the working budget.

plan.plan_project_budget.label: BUDGET CATEGORY
plan.plan_project_budget.description: The funding category the project draws on - blanket, discrete, or reimbursable.

plan.plan_project_budget.label: ASSET CLASS
plan.plan_project_budget.description: The asset class the finished work is capitalised into.

plan.plan_project_budget.label: BUSINESS UNIT
plan.plan_project_budget.description: The reporting business unit, as the portfolio register spells it.

plan.plan_project_budget.label: REGION
plan.plan_project_budget.description: The operating region the project sits in.

plan.plan_project_budget.label: STATE
plan.plan_project_budget.description: The state the work is performed in, which is what the rate case is filed against.

plan.plan_project_budget.label: PROJECT MANAGER
plan.plan_project_budget.description: Who owns delivery. PII.

plan.plan_project_budget.label: BUDGET LOCKED
plan.plan_project_budget.description: Whether the version is closed to further input for this project.

plan.plan_project_budget.label: LAST UPDATED
plan.plan_project_budget.description: When the row was last written by the cube.

plan.plan_project_budget.label: UPDATED BY
plan.plan_project_budget.description: Who last wrote the row. PII.

plan.plan_project_budget.label: SOURCE SYSTEM
plan.plan_project_budget.description: Which system the row came from - EPBCS for planned amounts, PeopleSoft for loaded actuals.

plan.plan_project_forecast.label: PROJECT CODE
plan.plan_project_forecast.description: The capital project key. Joins plan_project_budget.Project Code.

plan.plan_project_forecast.label: VERSION
plan.plan_project_forecast.description: The forecast version this row belongs to. Joins plan_version_master.Version.

plan.plan_project_forecast.label: SCENARIO
plan.plan_project_forecast.description: The cube Scenario member - Forecast for this table.

plan.plan_project_forecast.label: FORECAST VINTAGE
plan.plan_project_forecast.description: Which vintage produced the number: 3+9, 6+6 or 9+3.

plan.plan_project_forecast.label: FISCAL YEAR
plan.plan_project_forecast.description: The fiscal year the forecast is for.

plan.plan_project_forecast.label: ENTITY
plan.plan_project_forecast.description: The cube Entity member carrying the forecast.

plan.plan_project_forecast.label: ACCOUNT
plan.plan_project_forecast.description: The cube Account member. Joins plan_account_dim.Account.

plan.plan_project_forecast.label: PHASE
plan.plan_project_forecast.description: The project phase the forecast is held in.

plan.plan_project_forecast.label: FORECAST AMOUNT
plan.plan_project_forecast.description: The forecast for the year at this vintage, in dollars.

plan.plan_project_forecast.label: PRIOR VINTAGE AMOUNT
plan.plan_project_forecast.description: What the previous vintage forecast for the same year.

plan.plan_project_forecast.label: VINTAGE MOVEMENT
plan.plan_project_forecast.description: Forecast Amount less Prior Vintage Amount - what this vintage changed.

plan.plan_project_forecast.label: ACTUALS TO DATE
plan.plan_project_forecast.description: Spend recorded against the project up to the vintage cut month.

plan.plan_project_forecast.label: REMAINING FORECAST
plan.plan_project_forecast.description: Forecast Amount less Actuals To Date - what is still expected to be spent.

plan.plan_project_forecast.label: FORECAST VS WORKING BUDGET
plan.plan_project_forecast.description: Forecast Amount over the working budget for the same year.

plan.plan_project_forecast.label: CONFIDENCE BAND
plan.plan_project_forecast.description: The band the forecaster stated: firm, likely or indicative.

plan.plan_project_forecast.label: CUT MONTH
plan.plan_project_forecast.description: The month the vintage was cut at, which is what makes it a 3+9 or a 6+6.

plan.plan_project_forecast.label: PREPARED BY
plan.plan_project_forecast.description: Who prepared the forecast. PII.

plan.plan_project_forecast.label: REVIEWED BY
plan.plan_project_forecast.description: Who reviewed it before submission. PII.

plan.plan_project_forecast.label: SUBMITTED
plan.plan_project_forecast.description: Whether the vintage has been submitted for consolidation.

plan.plan_project_forecast.label: SUBMITTED ON
plan.plan_project_forecast.description: When it was submitted.

plan.plan_project_forecast.label: COMMENT
plan.plan_project_forecast.description: The forecaster free-text note carried with the row.

plan.plan_project_forecast.label: SOURCE SYSTEM
plan.plan_project_forecast.description: Which system produced the row.

plan.plan_monthly_spread.label: VERSION
plan.plan_monthly_spread.description: The version the phasing belongs to.

plan.plan_monthly_spread.label: SCENARIO
plan.plan_monthly_spread.description: The cube Scenario member the phasing is held under.

plan.plan_monthly_spread.label: FISCAL YEAR
plan.plan_monthly_spread.description: The fiscal year the months fall in.

plan.plan_monthly_spread.label: MONTH NUMBER
plan.plan_monthly_spread.description: The month ordinal within the fiscal year, 1 to 12.

plan.plan_monthly_spread.label: PHASE
plan.plan_monthly_spread.description: The project phase the month is planned in.

plan.plan_monthly_spread.label: MONTHLY PLAN
plan.plan_monthly_spread.description: The planned amount for this month, in dollars.

plan.plan_monthly_spread.label: MONTHLY ACTUAL
plan.plan_monthly_spread.description: The amount actually recorded for this month.

plan.plan_monthly_spread.label: MONTHLY FORECAST
plan.plan_monthly_spread.description: The current forecast for this month.

plan.plan_monthly_spread.label: MONTHLY VARIANCE
plan.plan_monthly_spread.description: Monthly Actual less Monthly Plan, in dollars.

plan.plan_monthly_spread.label: SPREAD PROFILE
plan.plan_monthly_spread.description: The phasing curve applied - linear, S-curve or manual.

plan.plan_monthly_spread.label: SPREAD LOCKED
plan.plan_monthly_spread.description: Whether the phasing is closed to further input.

plan.plan_monthly_spread.label: CUMULATIVE PLAN
plan.plan_monthly_spread.description: Planned amount accumulated from the start of the fiscal year.

plan.plan_monthly_spread.label: CUMULATIVE ACTUAL
plan.plan_monthly_spread.description: Recorded amount accumulated from the start of the fiscal year.

plan.plan_monthly_spread.label: LAST UPDATED
plan.plan_monthly_spread.description: When the row was last written.

plan.plan_version_master.label: VERSION
plan.plan_version_master.description: The version key, as every fact table spells it.

plan.plan_version_master.label: VERSION NAME
plan.plan_version_master.description: What the version is called on a form - Budget Final FY26, Forecast 6+6.

plan.plan_version_master.label: VERSION TYPE
plan.plan_version_master.description: Whether the version holds a budget, a forecast vintage or a medium-term plan.

plan.plan_version_master.label: SCENARIO
plan.plan_version_master.description: The Scenario member this version applies to. Joins plan_scenario_dim.Scenario.

plan.plan_version_master.label: CUT MONTH
plan.plan_version_master.description: The month the version was cut at.

plan.plan_version_master.label: FISCAL YEAR
plan.plan_version_master.description: The fiscal year the version plans.

plan.plan_version_master.label: STATUS
plan.plan_version_master.description: Where the version is: open, submitted, or locked.

plan.plan_version_master.label: IS LOCKED
plan.plan_version_master.description: Whether input is closed. The fact tables refuse writes against a locked version.

plan.plan_version_master.label: OPENED ON
plan.plan_version_master.description: When the version was opened for input.

plan.plan_version_master.label: LOCKED ON
plan.plan_version_master.description: When it was locked, where it has been.

plan.plan_account_dim.label: ACCOUNT NAME
plan.plan_account_dim.description: What the account is called in the chart.

plan.plan_account_dim.label: PARENT ACCOUNT
plan.plan_account_dim.description: The account this one rolls into. Self-join on Account.

plan.plan_account_dim.label: LEVEL NUMBER
plan.plan_account_dim.description: Depth in the account hierarchy, with 0 at the root.

plan.plan_account_dim.label: HIERARCHY PATH
plan.plan_account_dim.description: The full path from the root, as the cube renders it.

plan.plan_account_dim.label: IS LEAF
plan.plan_account_dim.description: Whether the member takes input, or only aggregates.

plan.plan_account_dim.label: AGGREGATION OPERATOR
plan.plan_account_dim.description: How the member rolls up: plus, minus or ignore.

plan.plan_account_dim.label: COST ELEMENT
plan.plan_account_dim.description: The cost element the account maps to in PeopleSoft.

plan.plan_account_dim.label: CAPITALIZABLE
plan.plan_account_dim.description: Whether spend on this account capitalises into the asset base.

plan.plan_account_dim.label: EFFECTIVE FROM
plan.plan_account_dim.description: First period the member is valid for.

plan.plan_account_dim.label: EFFECTIVE TO
plan.plan_account_dim.description: Last period it is valid for, where it has been retired.

plan.plan_period_dim.label: PERIOD
plan.plan_period_dim.description: The Period member key, including the accumulation members.

plan.plan_period_dim.label: PERIOD NAME
plan.plan_period_dim.description: What the period is called on a form.

plan.plan_period_dim.label: PERIOD TYPE
plan.plan_period_dim.description: Month, YearTotal, YTD or ITD - which is what makes a member an accumulation.

plan.plan_period_dim.label: FISCAL YEAR
plan.plan_period_dim.description: The fiscal year the period belongs to.

plan.plan_period_dim.label: QUARTER
plan.plan_period_dim.description: The fiscal quarter the period rolls into.

plan.plan_period_dim.label: MONTH NUMBER
plan.plan_period_dim.description: The month ordinal within the fiscal year, 1 to 12. Null on an accumulation member.

plan.plan_period_dim.label: IS ACCUMULATION
plan.plan_period_dim.description: Whether the member accumulates rather than holding one month.

plan.plan_period_dim.label: PERIOD END DATE
plan.plan_period_dim.description: The last calendar day the period covers.

plan.plan_phase_dim.label: PHASE NAME
plan.plan_phase_dim.description: What the phase is called in the stage-gate sequence.

plan.plan_phase_dim.label: PHASE ORDER
plan.plan_phase_dim.description: Where the phase sits in that sequence.

plan.plan_phase_dim.label: GATE REQUIRED
plan.plan_phase_dim.description: Whether leaving the phase needs a gate decision.

plan.plan_phase_dim.label: CAPITALIZABLE
plan.plan_phase_dim.description: Whether spend in this phase capitalises rather than expensing.

review_items.title: 'Working Forecast' proposed as a Plan Vintage member - create the node?
review_items.detail: epbcs.version carries Working alongside MTP2026_v3 and 3+9, so the profiler nominated it as a fourth vintage. It is not one. Working is a selector that resolves to whichever produced round is latest. Accepting it would let a query pin vintage=Working and get an answer whose meaning changes the day the next round is cut, with no version of the question having changed.
evidence: 6+6 and 9+3 are structurally zero - rounds not produced

review_items.title: Grantham Materials Laboratory, LLC - same firm across 3 projects, merge to one vendor?
review_items.detail: The firm is named in the party block of contracts filed under different projects. Both sides of the match were read out of a document, which makes this the lowest-confidence merge class in the graph. Approving it is what makes vendor concentration answerable at portfolio level; getting it wrong attributes one firm's exposure to another.
evidence: src_drive contract entity confidence 0.86 - lowest in the graph

review_items.title: Change order rider -> contract, matched on a contract number printed in the PDF
review_items.detail: 22 change orders were tied to their contracts by the contract number on the rider's face. Every AMENDS edge in the graph is extracted. A wrong match moves a priced amendment onto the wrong contract, which moves it onto the wrong project and the wrong vendor - three wrong answers from one bad join.

review_items.title: Caleb Kaltmeier and Dorothea Kaltmeier - merge on surname?
review_items.detail: The manager column carries two naming conventions and the normaliser handles the format. A surname collision is not an identity signal and the rule does not act on one. This sits in the queue as a declined match rather than being silently dropped, so a reviewer can see where the line is drawn.
evidence: format normalisation applies; surname-only matching does not

review_items.title: Authorized Amount resolved from the plan version chain (DR-5)
review_items.detail: There is no authorised-amount column. It is derived by taking the most recent approval date in northline_psoft.appr. On 2,426 projects the Most Recent Budget Plan and the Active Budget Plan disagree, so the rule decides which number the word 'authorised' means. The rule itself is still open (DR-5) and this queue item is where it gets settled.
evidence: 2,426 projects where Most Recent != Active Budget Plan
ds_psoft_appr is the connector's freshness floor - 7 days behind

review_items.title: Two BU codes aliasing one display label (DR-6)
review_items.detail: The entity-mapping upload carries an alias column in which more than one BU code can resolve to the same display label. Merging the codes would make BU rollups add up and make ownership unanswerable. They stay separate with the label aliased.

review_items.title: 'No State' nominated as a State - create the node?
review_items.detail: Every Shared Services Division row carries the literal string No State in attributes.state. The profiler saw a fifth distinct value and nominated it. It is a sentinel, not a place. Accepting it would hang a rate jurisdiction off something that has no commission and would quietly fold overheads into every spend-by-state answer.
evidence: attributes.state distinct values: Ardenia, Belmara, Corvale, Dunmoor, 'No State'
all 'No State' rows belong to Shared Services Division

pivot.title: 'Working Forecast' proposed as a Plan Vintage member - create the node?
pivot.detail: epbcs.version carries Working alongside MTP2026_v3 and 3+9, so the profiler nominated it as a fourth vintage. It is not one. Working is a selector that resolves to whichever produced round is latest. Accepting it would let a query pin vintage=Working and get an answer whose meaning changes the day the next round is cut, with no version of the question having changed.
pivot.why_pivot: This item changes what a word means, not what a row says. Accepting it silently would change the meaning of every answer that names it.
evidence: 6+6 and 9+3 are structurally zero - rounds not produced

sanity_checks.question: Which projects are forecasting above their approved plan, and by how much?
sanity_checks.verdict: Answerable - with a declared materiality floor
sanity_checks.verdict_body: The walk is Project -> MEAS:total_budget_working and Project -> MEAS:most_recent_budget_plan, differenced per project. It is answerable only with a floor stated on the face of the answer: 3,688 of 4,500 projects show a positive gap, so an unfiltered ranking is noise. At the declared floor - gap >= $2m AND >= 5% of plan - 2,966 projects qualify.
sanity_checks.plan:
MATCH (p:Project)-[:AGGREGATES_OVER]-(m:Measure)
WHERE m.id IN ['MEAS:total_budget_working','MEAS:most_recent_budget_plan']
RETURN p, gap = working - plan ORDER BY gap DESC

sanity_checks.question: What is our exposure to any single contractor across the portfolio?
sanity_checks.verdict: Answerable for the contract corpus only
sanity_checks.verdict_body: Vendor -> Contract -> Project resolves cleanly, but the corpus is 31 contracts across 5 projects. The honest answer names the vendor concentration inside that corpus and states that the other 4,495 projects have no contract documents in scope. Presenting it as portfolio exposure would be wrong.

context.meta: lowest node class in the graph

sanity_checks.plan: MATCH (v:Vendor)<-[:AWARDED_TO|ENGINEERED_BY]-(c:Contract)-[:DELIVERS]->(p:Project) RETURN v, count(DISTINCT p), sum(c.price_adj)

sanity_checks.question: Which projects hold an authorization but show no activity this year?
sanity_checks.verdict: Declined as asked - no natural instances
sanity_checks.verdict_body: Taken literally the question returns zero rows: projects In Planning carry both zero actuals and zero calendarized budget, so 'holds an authorization' and 'no activity' never co-occur in this extract. The answerable form is 'no FY26 actuals against a non-zero Active Budget Plan', and the answer must say it was relaxed.
sanity_checks.plan: MATCH (p:Project) WHERE p.active_budget_plan > 0 AND p.fy26_actuals = 0 RETURN p

sanity_checks.question: How much is committed but not yet spent?
sanity_checks.verdict: Declined - the commitment link has no instances
sanity_checks.verdict_body: PurchaseOrder is a schema type with zero members: the shipped extract carries no PO table. The chain Budget -> Authorization -> Commitment -> Actual is broken at the third link and the graph says so rather than substituting contract value, which is a different quantity at a different basis.

sanity_checks.question: What changed between the 3+9 forecast and the working view, and why?

metrics.name: Overrun amount one
metrics.description:
Overrun Amounts =
VAR ExceptionCategories =
    { "Network blankets", "Lead Capex Budget Category", "Meter blankets", "Plant roll-up" }
VAR ExceptionActuals =
    CALCULATE (
        SUM ( 'EPBCS_DATA_2'[FY26 YearTotal Actual] ),
        KEEPFILTERS ( 'EPBCS_DATA_2'[Budget Category] IN ExceptionCategories )
    )
VAR StandardActuals =
    CALCULATE (
        SUM ( 'EPBCS_DATA_2'[Inception to Date (ITD) Actuals] ),
        KEEPFILTERS ( NOT ( 'EPBCS_DATA_2'[Budget Category] IN ExceptionCategories ) )
    )
RETURNVVVVV
    ExceptionActuals + StandardActuals
        - SUM ( 'EPBCS_DATA_2'[Most Recent Budget Plan in PeopleSoft (Value)] )

ask_answers.question: Are we going to spend the authorized capital this fiscal year?
ask_answers.summary: No. The Working Forecast lands FY26 at $45.6m against a $48.1m working budget — $2.56m short.

blocks.markdown:
Read against the **Working Forecast** — the live, continuously-updated cut, not a forecast round — FY26 lands at **$45,555,684** against a working budget of **$48,114,647**. That is an underspend of **$2,558,963**, or 5.3% of the year.

The **3+9 forecast round** — the only formal round that ran this year — says **$48,087,579**, essentially on budget. The two disagree by **$2,531,895** because the 3+9 was cut in March and the working forecast has absorbed two months of actuals since. Which number you quote depends on whether you are reporting to a forecast round or to today.

blocks.title: FY26 monthly — actuals, Jan-calendarized budget, Working Forecast
blocks.note: Jan–May are actuals; Jun–Dec are forecast. The step at June is where the actuals series ends and the forecast begins, not a change in run-rate.

blocks.title: FY26 by region — budget against Working Forecast

blocks.markdown: Every region forecasts under budget, so this is not one region's problem. Actuals to May are **$17,622,670** against a phased budget of **$19,985,511** — already **$2,362,840** behind at the five-month mark, which is where the full-year shortfall comes from.

ask_answers.question: Where is authorized capital stalling — which stage of the chain is it stuck at?
ask_answers.summary: The chain breaks at commitment. Authorization is $452m, actuals are $96m, and the commitment stage between them is not in the connected data.

blocks.markdown:
The capital chain runs **Budget → Authorization → Commitment → Actual → CWIP → Capitalized**. Two of those six stages are present in the connected sources.

Authorization is **$452,300,192** across 4,500 projects (Active Budget Plan, `northline_epbcs.plan`). Actual cost inception-to-date is **$96,040,200** (`northline_psoft.gl`). Between them sits the commitment stage — purchase orders and contract obligations — and **there is no connected source for it**. `northline_psoft.appr` carries approval workflow, not commitment value.

So the honest answer is that 21.2% of authorized capital has reached actuals, and the remaining 78.8% is either committed or uncommitted — and this data cannot tell you which.

blocks.title: Capital chain — value present at each stage
blocks.note: Commitment, CWIP and Capitalized read zero because no source is connected for them. That is an absence of data, not a balance of zero.

blocks.markdown: **What to connect.** A commitment source — the PeopleSoft purchasing module or the contract register — would close the largest gap. A fixed-asset ledger feed would close CWIP and Capitalized. Until then, questions from HQ-20 through HQ-27 either decline or answer against a proxy, and the proxy is named every time.

ask_answers.question: How much of this year's plan is uncommitted with a quarter to go?
ask_answers.summary: Cannot answer — no commitment source is connected.

blocks.markdown:
This needs contracted commitment (K-07), and there is no source for it in the connected set. The four BigQuery datasets carry plan, general-ledger actuals, approval workflow and project attributes; none of them carries purchase-order or contract-obligation value.

**Uncommitted is not the same as unspent.** I can tell you that **$30,491,977** of the FY26 working budget is unspent as of 2026-05-31 (FY26 actuals close at May). I cannot tell you how much of that is already under contract, and reporting the unspent figure as though it were the uncommitted figure would overstate your procurement runway by whatever is already committed.

There is a related figure in the data — 207 budget lines flagged **Unencumbered**, carrying $41,911,645. That flag sits at business unit × budget category grain, not project grain, and it is a plan attribute rather than a commitment reading. It answers a different question (K-31) and must not be aggregated with project-grain figures.

ask_answers.question: Which projects hold authorization but show no activity this year?
ask_answers.summary: None at portfolio level — 0 projects match. But 732 In Planning projects have no actuals at all, which is a different condition.

blocks.markdown:
Testing FY26 actuals = 0 where FY26 working budget > 0 returns **0 projects**. Every project carrying an FY26 budget in this data has recorded at least some FY26 cost.

That result deserves suspicion rather than comfort. A real portfolio of 4,500 projects almost always has a stalled tail, and its absence here is a property of the fixture, not a finding about Northline.

The adjacent condition is real and larger: **732 projects In Planning** hold **$64,416,272** of active plan and **zero** inception-to-date actuals. Those are not stalled — they have not started, and they carry no FY26 working budget, so they do not meet the test above.

**Zero-activity and no-data are different states and this answer keeps them apart.** The In Planning cohort reads zero because the general ledger has no rows for those projects — an absence. If a project were genuinely stalled the ledger would carry rows with a zero FY26 sum, which is a presence. Nothing in this portfolio is in that second state.

ask_answers.question: What is the burn rate against current approved, by programme?
ask_answers.summary: Portfolio burn is 21.2% — the ratio of the sums. Lead Program runs at 38.8%, Federal PFAS at 13.2%.

blocks.markdown:
Portfolio burn is **21.2%** — $96,040,200 of actuals against $452,300,192 of active plan.

That figure is the **ratio of the sums**, not the mean of the project ratios. The mean of the 4,193 individual project ratios is **21.6%** — close here, but the two are different measurements and only the first one answers this question. The mean of ratios weights a $1.6k blanket the same as a $240k treatment plant.

blocks.title: Burn rate by programme (ratio of sums)
blocks.note: Each bar is Σ actuals ÷ Σ active plan within the programme.

blocks.markdown:
**Lead Program is the outlier at 38.8%** — nearly three times the PFAS rate. That is consistent with its delivery profile rather than alarming: all 342 of its dated projects carry a 2026 in-service date, so it is a programme in its spending year. **Federal PFAS at 13.2%** is early — its in-service dates spread to 2035 and peak in 2030.

207 projects carry no Active Budget Plan and are excluded from the denominator rather than counted as zero.

ask_answers.question: If spend continues at the current rate, where does the year land?
ask_answers.summary: A straight run-rate extrapolation lands FY26 at $42.3m — $3.26m below the Working Forecast.

blocks.markdown:
**This is an extrapolation, not a forecast.** Five months of actuals ($17,622,670 through May) annualise to **$42,294,409**. The planning system's own forecast — a different number with a different owner and a different method — says **$45,555,684**.

The extrapolation runs **$3,261,275 lower** because it assumes the first five months are representative. They are not: the Jan-calendarized budget phases 58.5% of the year into June–December, so a flat run-rate systematically understates a portfolio with a back-loaded construction season.

blocks.markdown: Use the extrapolation as a floor check, not as a number to report. If the year lands near the run-rate rather than the forecast, the question is why the back half never accelerated.

ask_answers.question: Where is forecast diverging from budget, by programme and category?
ask_answers.summary: Project-life forecast is $609m against an active plan of $452m — $157m above, concentrated in Plant large projects.

blocks.markdown:
Both coordinates, stated: **Forecast (EAC) × Project life, latest** reads **$609,163,329**. **Approved budget × Project life, active** reads **$452,300,192**. The gap is **$156,863,137**, or 34.7% above the approved book.

A gap that size across a whole portfolio is not a set of individual overruns — it is a systematic difference between how the planning system estimates lifetime cost and what the approval chain has authorized. Treat the portfolio number as a signal about the estimating basis and the project-level numbers as the actionable layer.

ask_answers.question: What is the variance against the current approved baseline, and against the original?
ask_answers.summary: FY26 actuals are $2.36m under the phased budget. Against the original approved book the portfolio-life forecast is $157m over.

blocks.markdown:
Two readings from one materialised set, because the comparison is lost if you re-execute against a single baseline.

**Against the current approved baseline (year to date):** actuals $17,622,670 against phased budget $19,985,511 — **$-2,362,840**, -11.8%.

**Against the original approved baseline (project life):** the approval chain has moved the baseline on **2,426 projects**, up $4,567,864 and down $-2,685,660 — net $1,882,204. Measured against the *original* rather than the moved baseline, project-life forecast exposure is **$156,863,137**.

blocks.title: Baseline movement — up, down, net
blocks.note: Offsetting movements are shown separately; netting them hides that 2,426 baselines moved at all.

blocks.markdown: The distinction matters because a project sitting exactly on its current approved baseline can be materially over its original one — that population is HQ-11, and it is where trust in the reporting actually breaks.

ask_answers.question: How far has the approved baseline moved since original approval, and who approved each move?
ask_answers.summary: 2,426 of 4,500 projects have a moved baseline — net $1.88m. Approver identity is only available for the five contract-pack projects.

blocks.markdown:
**2,426 of 4,500 projects** carry a Most Recent Budget Plan that differs from their Active Budget Plan. Upward movement totals **$4,567,864**, downward **$-2,685,660**, net **$1,882,204**.

**On the second half of the question — who approved each move — the data is thin and this answer says so.** `northline_psoft.appr` carries a plan-version sequence and a status per version, which is enough to walk the chain. It does not carry an approving authority for every project. The graph holds **103 plan-version nodes** covering the five contract-pack projects and their peers; for the rest of the portfolio the chain exists as two values (active, most recent) with no named approver behind the move.

On Quarrydown the baseline moved from **$239,836** to **$244,632** — $4,796 — and seq 2 is *approved but not yet active*, so today's reporting still runs against seq 1. A reader quoting the active plan and a reader quoting the most recent plan will disagree by that amount and both will be right.

**Note the as-of.** `ds_psoft_appr` runs 7 days behind the other datasets, so the plan chain is the oldest contributing source in this answer. Any figure derived from it inherits that floor — see HQ-33.

ask_answers.question: What did the forecast add between the 3+9 and the 6+6 cut for this fiscal year?
ask_answers.summary: Cannot answer — the 6+6 round was never produced for FY26.

blocks.markdown:
The 6+6 forecast round does not exist for FY26. `FY26 Forecast 6+6` is present as a column and empty on all 4,500 projects; the same is true of 9+3. Only the **3+9** round ran, alongside the continuously-maintained **Working Forecast**.

**This is an absence, not a zero.** Reporting the movement as $48,087,579 — 3+9 minus a 6+6 of nothing — would state that the re-forecast removed the entire year, which is false. The correct answer is that one of the two operands does not exist.

**What I can compare instead**, if you want the movement question answered against cuts that do exist: 3+9 at $48,087,579 against the Working Forecast at $45,555,684 — a movement of $-2,531,895. ask_answers.question: Which projects show no variance against current approved but material variance against original?
ask_answers.summary: 1,652 projects. $1.39m of variance was absorbed by baseline movement; $57.3m still sits above the moved baseline.

blocks.markdown:
**1,652 projects** have both had their baseline moved *and* still carry a material forecast gap against the moved baseline.

The baseline movement absorbed **$1,388,056** of variance on those projects — that is variance which no longer appears in any report run against the current approved figure. Above the moved baseline, **$57,339,507** is still exposed. Measured against the original approved book, total exposure on this cohort is **$58,727,563**.

**This is the question the domain actually asks**, and the answer names the movement rather than reporting a clean variance. A project whose baseline moved up by the same amount its forecast moved up reports zero variance and has consumed real capital.

ask_answers.question: How does the forward plan compare with the sum of project-life forecasts?
ask_answers.summary: The FY27–32 forward plan (MTP2026_v3) is $442m; the working budget over the same span is $465m — $23.4m higher.

blocks.markdown:
**Both spans stated.** The adopted forward plan is **MTP2026_v3** over **FY27–FY32**, totalling **$441,550,301**. The working budget across the same six years totals **$465,008,481**. The forward plan sits **$23,458,180** below the working view — 5.3%.

**The reconciliation does not close, and here is why it cannot.** A forward plan contains programme-level provisions for projects that do not exist yet as records, and it excludes project-level detail the working budget carries. The two are different objects measured over the same calendar, not two versions of one number. Anyone presenting the difference as a variance is asserting a reconciliation that the data does not support.

ask_answers.question: Which projects are trending to overrun, and by how much?
ask_answers.summary: 2,966 projects clear the materiality floor, carrying $107m. Ranked by the floor, not by magnitude.

blocks.markdown:
**The materiality policy first, because it determines the answer.** A project is admitted to this ranking when its forecast gap is **≥ $8,000** *and* **≥ 5% of its Most Recent Budget Plan**. Both conditions, not either.

Under that policy **2,966 projects** are trending to overrun, carrying **$107,486,253**. Without the floor the population is 3,688 projects and $110,477,798 — so the floor removes **722 projects and $2,991,546**, which is 2.7% of the gross figure and almost none of the decision.

A further **207 projects** carry no Most Recent Budget Plan at all. They have no baseline to overrun and are excluded from the population rather than ranked at zero.

blocks.title: Ranked by gap — top 15 over the materiality floor

blocks.markdown:
**Read the top of this list carefully.** The largest gaps by absolute value are Overhead projects, which are standing cost carriers rather than discrete builds — a project-life EAC against a project-life approval is a weak comparison for them. The first genuinely actionable rows are the Plant large projects and PFAS entries further down.

**On the portfolio-level bias.** 3,688 of 4,500 projects forecast above their baseline. A portfolio where four in five projects overrun is telling you something about the estimating basis rather than about delivery. Treat the ranking as relative, not as an absolute count of troubled projects.

ask_answers.question: Which movements have an explanation on record, and which are unexplained?
ask_answers.summary: 16 of 2,966 obliged movements have a message behind them — 0.54% by count, 1.18% by money. Correspondence is a drill-down, not a portfolio answer.

blocks.markdown:
**Denominator first, and it is the obligation floor.** 2,966 projects clear the materiality floor and are therefore obliged to carry an explanation.

**Coverage is 0.54%.** 16 of those 2,966 projects have at least one message in the connected mailboxes that resolves to them above the 0.70 publication floor. The other **2,950 have nothing** — not a low-confidence explanation, not a partial one. Nothing.

**Coverage by count and coverage by money are different numbers, and both belong here.** The 16 covered projects carry **$1,264,272** of the **$107,486,253** total material overrun — 1.18%. Quoting the money share alone would look better than the count share and would still be a rounding error. Neither supports a sentence beginning "correspondence tells us why the portfolio moved".

blocks.title: Material overruns — with and without a message
blocks.note: Computed over the obligation floor. The covered slice is the five contract-pack projects plus the eleven the internal project-controls thread names — it is where the mailboxes are, not where the risk is.

blocks.markdown:
**Why coverage is this low, and it is not a connection problem.** 4 mailboxes are in scope, not four thousand. Correspondence coverage is bounded by whose mail the platform is entitled to read, and that entitlement is deliberately narrow — permissions follow the source. Connecting every project manager's mailbox would raise coverage and would also mean the platform reads 4,500 projects' worth of private correspondence to answer a variance question. That trade is a governance decision, not a configuration one.

**What this changes about how to use the feature.** Correspondence answers *why did THIS project move* extremely well and *why did the portfolio move* not at all. A demo that shows the first and implies the second is setting up the question it cannot answer.

**Categories are read out of messages, never inferred from the shape of the movement.** Nothing in the four BigQuery datasets carries a variance-driver column. Two of those categories — *differing site conditions* and *existing asset worse than the bid documents assumed* — are the same failure at different stages, and they are kept apart deliberately: one is a subsurface surprise on new build, the other is a rehabilitation job finding the asset in worse shape. Merging them would hide which kind of estimating is failing.

ask_answers.question: Which contractors' projects overrun most often?
ask_answers.summary: Still no. Correspondence names 9 contractors across 18 projects — enough to say who is writing to us, nowhere near enough to rank overrun frequency across 4,500.

blocks.markdown:
**What connecting the mailbox did and did not fix.** Before, contractor identity reached the platform only through 25 vendor nodes extracted from contract documents on 5 projects. Correspondence adds sender identity on every message — so contractors are now named on **18 projects** rather than 5.

**That is still 0.4% of the portfolio, and the question asked about frequency.** A frequency claim needs a denominator per contractor: how many projects each one holds, not how many they wrote about. Nothing connected carries a contractor attribute on a project row, so the denominator does not exist and a ranking built on the numerator alone would rank whoever emails most.

blocks.title: Contractors appearing in correspondence (identity, not performance)

blocks.markdown:
**The trap this table is one step away from.** Kelso Ridge tops it on message count. Kelso Ridge also holds the largest and most complex package in the corpus, on a PFAS build with known subsurface risk. A contractor who writes four change-order notifications on a hard job and one who writes none on an easy one differ in the job, not the performance — and this table cannot tell those apart. **Read it as a directory of who is corresponding, not a scorecard.**

**What would make the question answerable** is unchanged from v1: a contract register carrying vendor identity on every project row, at portfolio scale. Correspondence is not a substitute — it is a sample of whoever happens to be in the 4 connected mailboxes.

ask_answers.summary: Both kinds now exist. 26 correspondence-sourced claims are on record and 0 authored annotations — every explanation in this tenant came from a message, and none from a person typing one.

blocks.markdown:
**The two provenances, and the count of each.** An explanation in Context Weave is either *authored* — a person opened the project and typed why it moved — or *extracted* — the platform read it out of a message or a document and is telling you what it thinks the text says.

In this tenant: **26 extracted, 0 authored.** Nobody has annotated anything. Every reason a reader sees on any screen is a machine's reading of somebody else's sentence.

**Why the distinction is load-bearing and not bookkeeping.** An authored explanation is a person's accountable statement — somebody's name is on it and they can be asked about it. An extracted one is a confidence-scored guess about text somebody else wrote for a different purpose. They are shown differently everywhere, including in export, and an extracted claim never silently becomes an authored one because a reader agreed with it.

**The 4 held claims are the part worth looking at.** Suppressed is not deleted. An extraction below the 0.70 floor is kept with its reason, because the suppressed list is how a reviewer sees what the floor is costing — and a floor nobody can audit is a floor nobody can tune.

**The Kaltmeier refusal is the important one.** A surname collision is not an identity. **No winner is picked in any of the three.** A controller asking this question is asking which system to trust, and the honest answer is that the graph does not know — it knows which system said what, and that is what it shows.

**The In Planning cohort is the honest surprise.** It holds $107,395,313 of working budget across 732 projects — the largest-looking deferral candidate in the portfolio — and its FY26 working forecast is **zero**. Nothing can be deferred out of a year it was never in. A scenario that showed those projects saving FY26 cash would be inventing the saving.

**Conflicting levers on one project are rejected, not averaged.** If a deferral lever and an acceleration lever both select the same project, the scenario refuses to run rather than netting them — a netted result reads as a single coherent plan when it is two incompatible ones. The user resolves the conflict; the engine does not guess.

**What this does not tell you.** Moving spend out of FY26 moves it into FY27, where the working budget is already $78,827,807 for the delivery and planning cohorts alone. Deferral is a phasing change, not a reduction — total programme cost is unchanged and escalation on the deferred work is not modelled here (see HQ-36).

ask_answers.question: What is the smallest set of projects we could defer to take $2 million out of FY26?
ask_answers.summary: **38 projects**, removing **$2,027,152** of H2 forecast. This is a candidate set under a stated rule, not a recommendation.

blocks.markdown:
**The rule, stated before the answer:** rank the 3,768 projects that carry July–December FY26 working forecast by the size of that H2 amount, and take from the top until the target is met. Nothing else is considered.

Under that rule, **38 projects** remove **$2,027,152** — 4.4% of the FY26 working forecast.

**What the rule ignores, and why that matters more than the answer.** The ranking is blind to compliance mandate, to in-service date, and to contractual commitment. 2,215 projects in this portfolio are marked *Mandated by Government Agency*; several sit in the 38. Deferring a mandated project is a regulatory decision, not a phasing one, and this engine has no basis on which to weigh it.

**Constraints a real candidate set would carry:** commitment status (unavailable — no PO data, see HQ-20), consent-order milestone dates (configuration, not a source column), and contractual notice periods (in the contract PDFs for five projects only).

**This is not a recommendation.** It is the smallest set satisfying one arithmetic rule, presented so the rule can be argued with. Changing the rule changes the set.

ask_answers.question: Are we replacing lead service lines fast enough to meet the mandated rate?
ask_answers.summary: **The replacement rate is not computable from connected data.** A mandated rate is lines per year against a known inventory; this package has projects and budget, and no service-line inventory at all.

blocks.markdown: **What the question needs, and what exists:**

blocks.title: Inputs required for a replacement rate
rows: Total service lines in the system
GL carries dollars, not line counts

blocks.markdown:
**The unknown-material trap.** Under LCRI a line of unknown material is treated as lead until proven otherwise, and inventory work reclassifies large numbers of them without replacing a single pipe. A dashboard that counts reclassifications as progress reports a replacement rate that is mostly paperwork. **An unknown-material line that becomes a known copper line is not a replaced line.** Any rate this platform eventually reports must state inventory completeness beside it, or the rate is uninterpretable.

**What can be said today.** 443 projects sit in the Lead Program with $39,429,861 of working budget, 28.3% of it spent. All 342 that carry a planned in-service date land in 2026. That is a spend position, and it is not a replacement rate — the two are related only by an assumed cost per line that nobody has supplied.

**What connecting a source would change.** A service-line inventory (typically GIS or the customer system) makes the numerator and denominator real. Until then this question has an honest partial answer and no complete one.
**Do not derive lines from dollars.** $11,165,571 divided by an assumed unit cost would produce a line count precise to four digits and grounded in nothing. The refusal is the answer.

Binding it to the sender's only active project would be a guess dressed as a resolution.

*Not read at all.* Two messages are in scope and unread. Their excerpt is literally `(not yet read)`. A runtime pull has a boundary and this is what the boundary looks like from the inside.

**None of these is a bug to be fixed by a better model.** The first two are messages that do not contain the information required to resolve them. A system that resolved them anyway would be inventing the missing part.

blocks.markdown:
**The media change-out claim.** `msg_029` says pilot data suggests change-out every 14 months rather than 24. That is not a capital cost this year and it does not move any figure in this package — which is exactly why it is interesting. It changes the life-cycle case on a plant whose capital case has already been made. Nothing in the connected data would ever surface it, because the connected data is a capital ledger and this is an operating assumption.

**The well-yield claim.** `msg_031` reports a well yield below the design basis and names **$19,200**, but its subject line names one project while its body describes another — a forwarded thread carrying last quarter's subject. The extractor resolved it to **Well Field Expansion** at 0.71 with 2 competing candidates, which is a resolution a reader should check rather than trust.

**What a reader should do with this.** Neither claim should be actioned on the strength of a message. Both should be taken to the person who wrote them. The value of the platform here is not that it settled anything — it is that two sentences buried in a mailbox surfaced against a forecast that was about to be filed, which is a thing no amount of ledger analysis would have done.

**Read the last column before the first.** The contractor classes and the internal classes are describing different things. ask_answers.question: Show me all the emails about the PFAS treatment programme.
ask_answers.summary: The platform will not search your mailbox. It reads mail to answer a business question and shows what it read; it is not a mail search tool, and the difference is a permissions boundary rather than a missing feature.

blocks.markdown:
**What is actually being asked for.** A list of messages matching a topic. That is a mailbox search, and if the platform returned one it would be re-publishing your inbox through a surface with different access rules than the mailbox has.

**Why that is not a small distinction.** Everything else in this product is governed by what a figure means and who may see that figure. Correspondence is governed by who may see the *mailbox*. Those two entitlements do not line up, and a mail-search screen inside an analytics product quietly resolves the mismatch in favour of the analytics product. So the platform never lists messages for their own sake — it lists the messages that produced a specific claim on a specific answer, and only to a reader whose own entitlement already reaches them.

**Ask it the other way and it works.** *Why has the PFAS treatment forecast moved?* or *what are contractors saying about the PFAS jobs?* — both read the same mail, resolve it against the projects the graph already holds, and return the claims with their senders, dates and confidence. What you cannot get is the raw thread list, and for that the mailbox is one click away and is the right place to look.

ask_answers.question: Who is raising problems — the contractors or our own team?
ask_answers.summary: Both, about different things. 19 messages from 9 contractor organisations, 14 from Capital Delivery. The contractors are claiming money; the internal team is warning about dates.

blocks.title: Where the correspondence comes from
blocks.note: Whole corpus, including the messages that did not resolve.

blocks.markdown:
**The split is the finding.** Every contractor message that carries an amount is establishing entitlement — differing site conditions, scope added after award, an existing asset worse than the bid documents assumed. Every one of those is a claim the owner has not agreed to, and the amounts should never be added to a forecast on the strength of the email.

**Internal messages carry almost no amounts and are the more useful half.** Capital Delivery writes about escalation, schedule slip and in-service dates that are not credible. Those do not move a cost line, they move a *date*, and a date moving is what puts an asset on the wrong side of a rate-case filing. The single highest-confidence internal extraction in the corpus (`msg_017`, 0.90) says outright that a job will not be in service before the filing — a sentence with no cost impact and a very large revenue one.

**What this is not.** 33 messages across 18 projects is not a communication-volume metric and should not be read as one. Four mailboxes are in scope out of an organisation that has hundreds. A contractor writing nothing here has almost certainly written to somebody whose mailbox is not connected.

ask_answers.question: Give me the variance reason for every project that is over budget.
ask_answers.summary: Not possible, and the shortfall is not close. Correspondence explains 16 of 2,966 material overruns — 0.54% by count and 1.18% by money. The other 2,950 have no explanation in any connected source.

blocks.markdown:
**Why the two percentages differ, and why both are quoted.** Coverage by money (1.18%) is more than double coverage by count (0.54%), because the projects people write about are the larger ones. Quoting only the money figure would flatter the platform; quoting only the count figure would understate what it reaches. Neither is anywhere near an answer to this question.

**$106,221,981 of material overrun has no reason attached in anything connected.** Not a low-confidence reason. Not a withheld reason. Nothing was written down anywhere the platform can read.

blocks.title: Material overruns: explained vs unexplained

data.label: No reason in any connected source

blocks.note: 2,966 material overruns. Materiality floor as declared on every ranking in this dataset.

blocks.markdown:
**What would actually close this, in order of honesty.** Connecting more mailboxes would help and would not fix it — the ceiling on mail-derived coverage is however many projects somebody happened to write a sentence about, and for a 4,500-project programme that ceiling is low. Text extraction on change-order documents would add reasons the mail only gestures at. A structured variance-reason field captured at forecast time is the only thing that reaches full coverage, and it is a process change rather than an integration.

**What the platform will do instead.** Ask it about a specific project and it will tell you what is known and what is not, which is the shape this capability actually has: a deep drill on the jobs that matter, not a column on a 4,500-row export. The honest way to use it is to rank by exposure first and read correspondence second.

document.title: What-if — Veolia CapEx
document.heading: What-if
document.subtitle: Stress the remaining forecast to complete without pretending to predict it. A what-if moves one attributable driver at a time — index-linked materials, labor, contingency — and recomputes only the slice the graph can tie to that driver. What it can't attribute is shown as a locked residual, not smeared across the answer. Nothing is forecast; every slice opens to its source. Authoring sets the scenario — which measures you watch, which drivers a case may move and how far, and its name. Runtime is where you move the sliders across cases, publish the complete scenario when it is worth sharing, and open any figure to the contract, timesheet or index feed it came from.

baseline.whyLine: A commitment-basis series and a projection-basis series in the same stack would be the mixed-coordinate failure. It is a reference line, and it is not included in the stack total.

blocks.note: One bar per category and the plan as a line over it, rather than two bars side by side. The gap between the bar and the line is that subtraction, and it is the shape the whole report is about.

quadrant.why: The horizontal line is zero variance, not a target. Both halves are problems and they are different problems: above it, money is going out faster than the plan allowed; below it, capital is not going into the ground on schedule, which defers the in-service date and therefore the recovery. The vertical line at 50% complete separates the projects where a decision still changes the outcome from the ones where it does not.

placeholder.unplaceableNote: 10 projects worth $272M sit in no tile at all: the date column holds the year-end default and no estimate was recorded. Nothing on this surface can place them in a month, and a filing decision is more exposed to these than to anything drawn above.

blocks.legendNote: Colour is execCategory from the CAPEX extract, ranked by value across the whole window so a category keeps its colour in every tile. Shares are of the months on screen, not of the programme.

basisPerMonth.rule: months at or before the portfolio as-of are record basis and read the recorded in-service date and capitalised value; later months are projection basis and read the forecast date and approved budget

blocks.overdueNote: 9 projects were due to enter service on or before 2026-03 with no recorded in-service date. They appear in no month tile — their due month is a record-basis month, which reads the recorded date they do not have — so they are listed here rather than dropped.

overdueTests.note: Two tests, listed together. The extract carries an overdue flag; the dates carry the same claim independently. Where they disagree, both results are kept and the row says which test found it — a flag that misses a project the dates condemn is a finding about the source, not a rounding difference.

footing.note: The cells foot to the 60-project sample. The figures above the calendar are declared over the whole programme, so they are larger and the two are not meant to reconcile.

blocks.whyNoTotal: No window total. The window spans record and projection basis, and one total across it would add a recorded quantity to a projected one.

peak.note: The declared peak month 2027-01 is outside this window. It is a programme figure over 4500 projects; the cells below foot to the 60-project sample, which is why the two disagree.

blocks.note: Each month tile states its own basis, and the two bases read different fields — a recorded in-service date with its capitalised value, or a forecast date with its approved budget. A single total across the window would silently add a recorded quantity to a projected one, which is the failure this report exists to avoid.

reports.note: The schedule covers the ledger blocks only. The line-item explanations and the two correspondence blocks are runtime: they are read under the asking session's own mailbox entitlement at the moment the report is opened, and nothing from them is cached. Two people opening this report an hour apart can legitimately see different messages, and neither inherits the other's access. Caching them nightly would produce an extract owned by whoever ran it, which is the permission leak the runtime class exists to avoid.
